messages:
leo: Heads up, ap-southeast1 started throwing up a lot of GPU pod evictions ~45m ago. Eviction rate ~2x baseline and many Pending->Preempt cycles.

tess: Saw it. Attaches to GPU devices are timing out; node kubelet logs show repeated 'attach timeout' and kernel conntrack nearing max.

mai: Metric snapshot: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count ~126k / 131072 and `device_attach_duration_ms` p95 jumped to 18s.

leo: Workloads impacted are fractional-GPU tiny-gang jobs with strict requiredDuringScheduling affinity + hard anti-affinity, so packing fails and scheduler preempts lower-priority pods to free whole nodes.

tess: Short-term playbook: 1) bump nf_conntrack_max on subset of nodes, 2) temporarily relax anti-affinity to soft for tiny-gang, 3) add +1 warm GPU node if congestion persists. Which to try first?

mai: I'm for bumping conntrack canary first. sysctl example: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144`. We can roll via a privileged daemonset to 10% nodes and watch `conntrack_drops`.

leo: I'll open an incident if we see preemptions continue after canary window.

infra-bot: INC-2026-045 created: "apse1 attach-chain timeouts -> scheduler preempt cascade" assigned to eng-platform.

oncall: If canary isn't stable in 20m, ops will provision +1 on-demand GPU node in ap-southeast1 for 6h.
